correctness.rationale: Minimality on a Cantor space makes T aperiodic. The only candidate S-preimages of T^b x are x (if p(x)=b) and T^d x (if p(T^d x)=a). Exactly one exists iff membership in {p=b} is the same at x and T^d x; this gives both directions using bijectivity on the T-orbit and compactness for the inverse. On the integer orbit each increasing S-orbit crosses the cut at 0 exactly once. There are a guaranteed crossings plus k positions of jump b in the next block of length d; periodicity makes the count T-invariant and minimality makes it constant. Translates of a T^d-minimal set are equal or disjoint and their union is X; the number of clopen components divides d. For the upper bound, conjugation of T^2 by the swap of disjoint clopen levels A and TA realizes p=3,1,2 on A,TA,T^2A respectively and only positive jumps 1 through 3 elsewhere; T^2 is minimal by total minimality. Independently replayed 48,960 cyclic assignments and 6 conjugation proxies, without executing verify.py. Finite cycles corroborate the bounded classification/construction only, not the Cantor or universal minimality assertions.
